requirements_summary: Scale: target index = 30M-70M dense embeddings across monorepos, incremental commit-level updates every 4-8 hours.
Latency: tail latency SLO for top-10 reranked responses <= 150ms for 95th percentile; prefer <100ms for cache hits.
Throughput: 200 QPS sustained during business hours, burst to 1k QPS on release days.
Cost sensitivity: aiming for <$0.002 per query equivalent for typical rerank+embed pipeline; need cost/latency tradeoff visibility.
Model preferences: open-models acceptable if quantized (8-bit/4-bit) and verified for reranking quality; fallback routing to smaller models during capacity issues.
Indexing: frequent incremental re-indexing with ability to parallelize ingestion and zero-downtime canonical index swaps.
Search quality: need tuned reranker with pairwise/triplet retraining support and evaluation hooks tied to PR-based test sets.
Security: SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning, audit logs per request, customer-managed KMS for keys, EU data residency for production clusters.
Operations: want per-route cost telemetry, token-level billed breakdown, and automatic fallback policies for availability degradation.
notes: Initial pain: in-house Milvus cluster works but ops cost is high, unpredictable latency on large indices during reindex windows.
Quote from Elliot: 'We need indexing to be invisible to dev velocity — reindexes can’t block CI and must be incremental.'
Redwood fit hypothesis: Dedicated pools for vectors + Optimize suggestions to reduce token cost on reranker calls; Private for EU residency.
POC asks: run a 72-hour soak with 50M vectors, 6-hour incremental updates, simulate 200 QPS steady / 1k burst; provide cost projection and latency histogram.
Engineering notes: interested in KV cache prefixing for repo-level queries, and continuous batching to improve GPU utilization without blowing tail latency.
SAML: they use Azure AD; need example SAML metadata and SCIM user provisioning flow documented. SecOps also wants user-level audit events retained 12 months.
Data handling: code is treated as sensitive IP; will only allow on-prem/private for some customers; global customers require EU-resident clusters.
Reranking approach: two-pass — ANN top-200 by embeddings then lightweight cross-encoder rerank for final top-10; want Redwood to support both stages and show cost split per stage.
Ask to AE: connect them to Solutions Eng to discuss quantization tradeoffs and to Research for reranker evaluation framework.
Competitive concerns: they trialed Pinecone + custom cross-encoder but cost to reach 95th-percentile latency was too high; also evaluated Milvus + FAISS but ops effort is blocker.
